main_text.p: ra iudicium feruorum fidelium & prudē tum, aliud malorum.

Illi enim suo munere funguntur, alimenta famulitio Domini in tempore dā tes.Hi autem in cordibus suis dicunt:χρο-νίζει ὁ λύγιος ἐλθεῖν: ac conseruos cædunt,& cum ebrijs edunt & bibunt. Matthæi 24. 45.46.47.

Quid? an'ne iudicabimus, Harmostas quosdam,conseruos suos(quasi de plau-stro eis maledicendo, dentata charta eos confodiendo, πονηροί in exilium agen-do,nulla uirtutum & fidelitatis in officio præstitæ ratione habita) ufqueadeò inhu-maniter tractaturos esse,nisi in cordibus suis diceret: Tardat Dominus noster ad-uentum? Et quis non uideat culinarum aulicarum nidore & pemmatis delica-tos Hierophantas quosdam sic deliniri & inefcari,ut cum ebrijs perpotare,& cō seruos cædere malint, quàm cum his de pietatis summa συνωνοιμ instituere? Sed uidet hæc Deus, qui etiam die quo non exspectat, ueniet: & nisi prius resipiscat (quod sanè toto pectore illis opto) sepa-rabit eos,partemq; eis assignabit cum hy-pocritis. Matth.24.51.

page.notes: Greek words in the text are transcribed from a small, worn print and are uncertain: "χρο-νίζει ὁ λύγιος ἐλθεῖν" (printed as ꝯ-marked Greek, first word read as "ζ..." with a superscript), "πονηροί" and "συνωνοιμ" are doubtful; the last Greek word may be "συνοικοῦ" or similar. Long s has been normalised to s/s-free text here where clear; the page shows "s" in places and it is rendered as s in the Latin. "Nos," is the last word at the lower right, possibly a signature or catchword fragment. The running head is "IN HABACVC CAP. II." as printed.
